claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a random BCC solid solution.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has severe local lattice distortion caused by chemical disorder.
The random alloy has a broad, low-frequency phonon DOS and short phonon mean free paths because of mass-fluctuation and strain-field scattering.
Controlled annealing or thermal history can induce chemical SRO and HfTi/TiZr cluster nucleation in HfNbTaTiZr.
HfTi and TiZr clusters can percolate into ordered B2-like structures.
A temperature range of 600–900 K is sufficient for SRO ordering while remaining below the solvus and preserving the BCC framework.
Percolating B2-like HfTi/TiZr clusters locally regularize atomic positions and reduce atomic-size-mismatch and elastic-strain variance.
The transition from a random alloy to ordered binary domains reduces RMS lattice distortion.
Reduced lattice distortion shifts high-frequency phonon DOS peaks to higher frequencies because of stiffer effective bonding.
The DOS shift associated with ordering increases phonon group velocity.
Ordered B2-like domains act as phonon-scattering centers.
Reduced background scattering from lattice distortion and coherent percolation pathways outweigh domain scattering, producing a net increase in lattice thermal conductivity.
The SRO-ordered state will have higher lattice thermal conductivity than the random state.
The ordered state will exhibit narrower high-frequency phonon DOS peaks and lower Debye-Waller factors for the relevant species or binary environments.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has ultra-low, glass-like lattice thermal conductivity because of lattice distortion and mass variance.
Below the SRO-cluster percolation threshold, the alloy retains random-alloy-like low conductivity.
Above a sufficiently high degree of ordering, macroscopic phase separation can cause conductivity to decrease through strong interface scattering.
Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti alloys can contain ordered B2 and/or L21 precipitates within a disordered BCC matrix.
The HfTi/TiZr percolation threshold has not been experimentally verified in HfNbTaTiZr.
It remains uncertain whether distortion reduction from B2 ordering outweighs the interface-scattering penalty in HfNbTaTiZr.
